doc: Words a newcomer may not know (issue #69): `aka` lists how the word appears on screen; the design screen adds a word's meaning when an option shows it, and How to play lists them all. Texts are English; Spanish in i18n/glossary.csv.

orbit.meaning: The path a craft follows around a planet, falling all the time but moving sideways fast enough to keep missing the ground.

LEO.meaning: Low Earth orbit: a few hundred km up, a lap every hour and a half. Easy to reach, but the thin air slowly drags craft down.

SSO.meaning: Sun-synchronous orbit: passes near the poles and crosses each place at the same hour of sunlight every day, so pictures can be compared day after day.

GEO.meaning: Geostationary orbit: 35,786 km above the equator, where one lap takes a day, so the craft stays over the same spot.

L2.meaning: A point 1.5 million km away on the far side of the Earth from the Sun, where a telescope can keep the Sun, Earth and Moon behind its shield.

Δv.meaning: Delta-v: how much a craft can change its speed with its fuel. Every move (climbing to an orbit, staying in it) costs some.

band.meaning: The higher the frequency (UHF, S, X, Ka), the more data per second, but the more exact the aim of the antenna must be.

CubeSat.meaning: A small satellite built from 10 cm cubes: a 3U is three cubes in a row. Cheap and quick to build.

eclipse.meaning: The part of each lap spent in the Earth's shadow, where solar panels make nothing and the battery keeps the craft alive.

reaction wheels.meaning: Wheels spun by motors inside the craft: speeding one up turns the craft the other way, so it can aim without fuel.

star tracker.meaning: A small camera that recognizes star patterns to know exactly where the craft points.
